headline: ICE shot him in the back. Now he's charged with assault.
summary: Federal prosecutors on Tuesday charged Wilber Garces Perez, the Venezuelan delivery driver an ICE agent shot in Austin on September 20, with assaulting an officer. The affidavit says his side mirror hit an agent as he drove off. He says an SUV spun his car before the shot. The agent who fired wore no body camera. He faces up to 20 years.

cover_question.q: Why did the police shoot him?

cover_answer: The agent says the car hit him first. The driver says no.
table_question: Two people tell one story two ways. No video. Who do you believe?

5-7.script: A man in Texas was shot by an officer and hurt. Now the officer's side says he did something wrong first, and he says they did. A judge will listen to both, like a teacher hearing two kids tell one story two ways. He is alive, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Two kids, one story: the only frame a six-year-old needs here.
5-7.why_long: Shielded: a shooting is a story a six-year-old can do nothing with, and they read your face before your words. If it reaches them, the script keeps it to one thing they know, two kids telling a teacher one story two ways, and ends on the fact that he is alive. Expect "did he die?" No. He is hurt, and doctors are looking after him.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: On September 20 an ICE agent in Austin shot a Venezuelan driver in the back as he drove off from a traffic stop. On Tuesday prosecutors charged the driver, saying his mirror hit an agent as he left. He says an SUV rammed him first. The agent who fired wore no camera, so it's two stories and no tape.
8-12.why: Stop, mirror, shot, charge: a chain with the referee missing.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect and whether adults follow their own rules, so the script gives them the chain in order, then the gap: the agent who fired wore no camera, after ICE said all of them would by the end of September. A playground row with no referee is a fairness call they make weekly. Expect "who's lying?" Unknown.

13-17.script: Can the person who got shot be the one charged? Prosecutors say yes: Wilber Garces Perez's mirror hit an agent as he drove off, so it's assault. He says an SUV spun his car before the agent fired, and that agent wore no camera. Second: in past cases, footage undid the agents' account. What would you need to see?
13-17.why: Two accounts and one missing camera.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two accounts at once and reason about evidence that is not in the room, so the script gives them both versions, the agent with no camera, and AP's pattern of past agent claims undone by footage. The question is what would settle it. Expect "why is the shot guy charged?" The charge is about the mirror, not the shot.

5-7.q: Why did the police shoot him?
5-7.a: Grown-ups disagree about that, and a judge will sort it out. He is alive, and doctors are looking after him.

8-12.q: Who decides who's telling the truth?
8-12.a: A judge and a jury, later. Two accounts, no video of the shot.
Held by US Marshals. Up to 20 years, if a court finds him guilty.

13-17.q: Can they shoot you and charge you?
13-17.a: Yes. The charge is about the mirror, before the shot.

13-17.q: Why wasn't the agent wearing a camera?
13-17.a: The affidavit doesn't say. ICE promised cameras for all by month's end.
